what: The heuristic precomputes a directed routing model by discovering loc/visited facts semantically, identifying the depot structurally, resolving load and vehicles IDs, and extracting direct, via-depot, and return costs primarily from grounded operators. For each state it finds the current location and unvisited set, checks fleet-capacity feasibility when exact resource constants are available, chooses a capacity-feasible first transition from the current location, estimates directed continuation and final-return costs, and adds explicit capacity-reload and fleet-pressure components.
why: The representative instances are fleet-limited capacitated routing problems with heterogeneous demands, so load, remaining demand, used vehicles, residual capacity, and required depot reloads directly affect the estimate. Their dense explicit travel-cost matrices motivated operator-based directed cost reconstruction and cheap precomputed local connection summaries. The domain has materially different direct visit and visit-via-depot actions, so the first transition and reload component model those alternatives separately. Because the family has many customers but a small fleet, evaluation is linear rather than repeatedly sorting or constructing an MST. This is more informative than customer count because it uses actual directed travel and state resources; more informative than summed depot distances because it accounts for the current anchor and customer-to-customer links; and more informative than a purely geometric estimate because it detects fleet-capacity dead ends and charges for depot reloads.
instance_patterns: Fleet-limited capacitated routing with multiple depot reloads on low-capacity instances
Dense explicit pairwise travel costs that are usually symmetric in examples but are treated as directed
Heterogeneous customer demands that make residual load and packing pressure important
Dozens of customers, favoring linear per-state evaluation with task-level precomputation
Single-depot goals requiring every customer to be visited and a final return to the depot
design: Geometric routing estimate over the current unvisited set
Capacity/resource bound using remaining demand, current load, capacity, and remaining fleet
complexity: O(n) per state, where n is the number of customers; static matrix construction and operator scanning occur only in new().
fallbacks: Missing direct arcs are first recovered from exact travel-cost PNE names and initial values. Missing via-depot arcs are then synthesized only when both directed depot legs are known. Missing capacity, demand, or max-vehicles names use permissive defaults and disable or weaken resource terms without preventing routing evaluation. Construction fails clearly if a customer lacks a usable depot outgoing or return arc.
known_limitations: The continuation estimate uses precomputed minimum directed outgoing links and therefore can select links through customers already visited or create disconnected subtours.
Aggregate demand determines the estimated reload count and does not solve the full heterogeneous bin-packing problem.
The fleet-pressure term is a deliberately non-admissible tie breaker and may overestimate or reorder states imperfectly.
